You are the leader of a 90-man rebel unit dedicated to defeating Lincoln.

To do this, they brought your men to the planet Ganama 4, from which you can go indirectly to all planets of the forbidden solar system on Lincoln's home planet. For this purpose, the men are in the so-called "speed gnats", in small docking capsules that cannot be seen by any radar. The speed gnats can be docked while space dreamers are waiting for their permission to start. With the space transporters, the men each travel one planet further towards the forbidden planet.

Even before the last female transport has reached the forbidden planet, the speed gnats must be in the atmosphere, since the planet will then be surrounded by a protective shield.

The landing site closest to Lincoln is guarded by some vehicles and equipment that a sniper already placed on the forbidden planet will try to take out so that the Speed ​​Gnats can land. The defense vehicles are unmanned and are almost unlimited.

There are space scooters behind the landing field, with which the men can fly to the city. At the same time, another group with watercraft has to penetrate the cave system protected by technical security measures, where the next woman victim is waiting.

The “tripsies” live at the place of the three gates behind which the women are. A tripsi is a wooden being who can open the gates with his flute playing. If you control a Tripsy, you can free the women.

Meanwhile, the other group will try to break into the city. To do this, you have to take one of your men over the city using a hot air balloon. There he can parachute to the landing site in the city.

The man will fly the surface of the city with a space scooter until he finds the location of Lincoln. The computer has three internal inputs through which the woman victims are brought to it.

168890.overview: Linking Logic is an educational game meant to improve children's logical reasoning and planning skills. The aim of the game is to guide one of two children (Buddy or Betty) through the five floors of a building, from the top to the bottom. This is done by flying a bird who can place various objects (bridges, springs, walls and ladders) along the path. These are needed to prevent the child from falling through holes or changing its direction. Once the objects have been placed the game can be started and the child will start walking. As they walk a button has to be pressed as they pass patterned tiles. Those tiles will then be placed in spaces on the bottom floor. If a tile is missing when the child reaches the bottom floor the game is lost.

168893.overview:
Little People Bowling Alley is a 1-2 player trivia/bowling game for multiple systems.

Each player controls a little person, who is positioned at a bowling lane. The player rolls the ball, and tries to knock as many pins as possible. There are 2 balls per frame with 6 pins, and a total of 10 frames in a game. On difficulty 1, the player always rolls straight, but on higher difficulty, the player must coordinate their button presses with character movement to bowl straight ahead.

168894.overview: A train-yard strategy game. You can choose to play the Flat Yard version or the Hump Yard version. Locomotive Switcher brings and operating railroad layout to the Commodore 64 compute screen. The micro-layout consists of mainline, six switches and seven loading areas. Sophisticated car motion logic simulates train movements to a degree not possible on "real" model railroad layouts.

168895.overview: If you like mazes, you'll love Logic Levels. First you tell the Magic Hand where to put the walls, bridges and springs to guide the ball through the maze. The more prizes it hits, the more points you will score. But that's just the beginning!

168896.overview: Indians have kidnapped your comrades. You, the last of the company, venture directly into the enemy's cave, into the Indian camp. In the desert, in the midst of hostile territory.

168897.overview: Looney Balloon is a side view single screen game where you have to control a balloon from it's starting position and navigate it through a path to land on a landing-pad while collecting all the objects on screen over various levels. The balloon will sway at all times and gravity pulls it down so you must keep the balloon up while moving it around the screen. Each screen must be completed within a time limit and the walls cannot be touched or you lose one of five lives if you run out of time or touch the walls. There are five skill levels (Novice, Pilot, Instructor, Test pilot and Kamikaze) with a higher skill level meaning the balloon sways and falls faster.

168916.overview: You are an explorer deep in the jungles of South America searching in a Lost City of the Maya for relics. There are ten of these valuable Maya relics to find scattered around the surrounding area in buildings and temples. The quest won't be easy as there are plenty of traps and red herrings to be discovered. The Lost City is a graphic text adventure where pictures show you each location while text describes what you can see. You type in commands with the keyboard to control your hero and interact with various locations.

168917.overview: Lost in the Labyrinth is a top view maze game where you are an explorer and it is your quest to move around the labyrinth and find staircases to move up the levels before finding the exit. As you move around you will encounter various creatures and if you touch one then you are shown a close-up of you and the monster and you must fight it to kill it. If you are killed by a monster then you lose one of four lives, and when they are gone, you are given a score and a comment on your attempt. There are also various objects that can be found and used in your quest and these include hammers, spears and bombs. Control of your hero is done with a light pen which allows you to touch the screen and use dots to move as well as use and drop objects found. This game is designed to be played with a lightpen attachment.

168918.overview:
This multi-genre game is based on the famous comics series about Lucky Luke, a good cowboy who draws his gun and shoots quicker than his shadow.

It was decided to construct a railway line to connect the East and West of the United States. Two companies argued about the establishment of this line. You were chosen to protect the quality of the line and to do not give it away to the competitor.

In the beginning, Lucky Luke should move around the town and find out the bandits preventing him from travel on the train. During arcade shooting he should shoot all of them on the streets and inside the saloon.

After train stops in front of the boulder on the rails, Lucky Luke has to find the way to this boulder to blow it up with a bomb collecting the useful items and using them in adventure mode. During these actions he'll encounter four Daltons and Apache's leader.

The next trial is a puzzle, where Lucky Luke has to connect the branch lines for the train switching the points on the railway.

And the last one is to solve the problem of water between Comanches and the Ranch owners in the place where quality will be checked finally.

168920.overview:
A Uridium clone, space based shoot'em up where you are the commander of a mighty interplanetary spaceship whose mission is to patrol areas of the cosmos where there are enemy alien fleets. Each area gets you closer to the heart of the fleet, and so increases in difficulty. 

Released as Planet Six in Italy in Go Games n.44 (giugno 1989).

169090.overview:
Coed -Elyon, is under threat from an evil spell, which is caused by a sacred stone, known as the Brex Rune. As Xandra, a fearless female fighting warrior. You must locate and destroy the deadly Brex Rune, heavily guarded by an evil demon. If you encounter the demon, you must find a way to destroy the stone. That stone can be found at Yaxley Tower. If you are to get this far, you must fight hard, encounter Faes, which will give you spells in which will help you on your quest. Good luck. The fate of Coed-Elyon depends on you.

Won second place in the Official C64 SEUCK Comp 2019.

169180.overview:
In the mid-'70s, an unusual phenomenon took place: two Americans, Willie Crowther and Don Woods wrote the first text adventure game: it was the Original Adventure and was written in Fortran for a DEC PDP-10 and occupied more than 300 K of memory. It gathered a cult following from the elite programmers who knew how to connect to the data bank where it was located, and like all cults, it had its first "martyrs"; several important programmers were fired after becoming "addicted" to it, found playing it late at night while understood to be working overtime instead.

In the United States it was the base that inspired Scott Adams to begin with his famous adventures. In Great Britain, Peter Austin, founder of Level 9, the most prestigious English adventure game company, confessed to be impelled by it from his beginnings as a game designer (one of his first adventures was a version of the Original Adventure). In Spain, there was a similar story, since the first Spanish company dedicated exclusively to text adventures (Aventuras AD), made its reputation based on a game curiously called "La Aventura Original" (yes, based on the legendary one), the fruit of 8 months of investigation and work.

This version, aside from being in Spanish, has with several points worth mentioning, such as having more than 100 detailed locations with graphical illustrations; a special routine of exit descriptions (indispensable for guiding the adventurer through this complex world); and the possibility of using accents, "ñ"'s and opening interrogation and exclamation signs. As well, every object of your inventory is described in text and graphic form. The characters also use the PSI system, so they are not mere objects with human names, but will listen to you and respond -- but most importantly, will act according to how you treat them.
A two part adventure based on Colossal Cave Adventure consists of "Part I - La Busqueda" & "Part II - El Encuentro" (Password for 2nd part is BATRACIO) Published in Dinamic's Metal Action game pack.

170937.overview: A train simulation with a touch of train management but focused on the train engineer experience.

171500.overview:
The Last Warrior is a space shooter is controlled from the cockpit of a scout ship - the last one in its squadron, following a particularly vicious alien attack; only a pair of frontal-mounted lasers and a finite amount of shield energy stand between the player and waves of relentless enemy fighters. As alien vessels zoom across the viewscreen, they must be hunted down using the lasers, before they get the chance to fight back. Every shot had better count, since firing uses up your precious shield energy. Enemy fire will deplete the shields as well; one hit without a shield, and you'll be sucking vacuum. When it's all over, your performance will be scored, along with a display of your hard-earned military rank.

Published in COMPUTE! 1985/09 (Issue #64).

171506.overview:
Puzzler in which you must line up the lemons next to each other to beat each level. But all is not as simple as it sounds. A puzzle game published in Magic Disk 64 1994/06. 

That’s Bodo with the excavator, and he’s still excavating, "it sounds like every year at many carnival events.
At Lemon Blues you take on the role of a bulldozer driver. Your goal? Very easily! You have to line up the three yellow lemons with the help of the purple fruits (horizontally or vertically). You can control your excavator with the joystick in port # 2. Also:

Lemon movement Move to the fruit and press fire. The fruit will stop at the next wall or the next lemon. Destroying the purple lemon First press fire and then in the direction where the purple lemon is. Attention! It must be on a wall or another lemon. Destroying the Enemies One hit with a lemon is enough to kill these fellows. After each level you will receive a code word that you can enter again the next time you start.

171507.overview: This is a dueling shooter game. You vs. your best frenemy or against the C64.

171508.overview:
An action game from Harald Sprung and published in Magic Disk 64 1996/01. Leppard is a diamond collecting robot. In order to get from one level to the next, he has to show twenty diamonds - not an easy task, since in addition to the sparkling stones there are also four malicious opponents in the labyrinth who only have one thing in mind: to touch Leppard so that he evaporated in a big green cloud. 
 

Leppard is controlled through a total of ten levels with one opponent, but he not only has the four villains already mentioned, but also a sometimes very tight time limit. In order to at least defend himself against the numerous opponents, Leppard can plant a bomb at the push of a button. However, this can only be done standing up. Who is able to release the fuse of such a dangerous object in a full sprint? However, you have to be particularly careful, because enemies that have been blown up will return to the field in a few moments!

171511.overview:
The Apollo Lunar Module, or simply lunar module (LM, pronounced "lem"), originally designated the Lunar Excursion Module (LEM), was the lander spacecraft that was flown from lunar orbit to the Moon's surface during the U.S. Apollo program. It was the first crewed spacecraft to operate exclusively in the airless vacuum of space, and remains the only crewed vehicle to land anywhere beyond Earth.  
 
In this Lunar Lander style game you need to avoid the subsurface perils to reach your landing goal intact.

171512.overview: Published in Game On 1995/02. A Bomberman style action game. To finish a level, you have to destroy all goals and ghosts with bombs. But watch out, as long as there's a goal left, for every destroyed ghost a new one will appear. Destroyed ghosts who can reappear will come back stronger. And when the timer runs out...well may God have mercy.

171513.overview: The sequel to the Alternative Software game, Lethal from 1988, and done by the same creators. This 2004 version is still a shooter, but more in line with a game like Bounder, except horizontally scrolling instead of vertically scrolling.

171514.overview:
Lethal Zone was developed by Michael Beier for Double Density, and was published in Golden Disk 64 1991/10, and in Golden Disk 64 - Gold Edition.

Lethal Zone is a German horizontal shooter in the same vein as the R-Type series of games. You control a spaceship and you shoot enemy ships and obstacles, while avoiding projectiles and crashing on any surface. Holding the fire button and releasing it increases the power of your shots, while hitting it repeatedly lets out a stream of them. The destroyed enemies occasionally leave behind power-ups that can be collected. They increase and modify the power of your shots. You start with 5 lives, and at each 50.000 points you receive an extra one. The games has four levels, each with a unique "boss" enemy at the end.

171516.overview:
You have 6 Gyro-copters and must make your way, safely though the caves, avoiding all obstacles, giant blocks, falling weights, cave walls and trolley cars. Hit even one and you lose your life and have to start the current cave over.

Published in Italy in Peek n.16 (aprile 1986) under the name Sea Chopper.

171517.overview:
The power to Earth is all supplied by one huge power station that orbits the planet but a problem has arisen, a bug in the computer system has mutated all the computer circuits and made them aware of themselves and worst of all, became alive. It has decided for reasons still unknown, turned all the power off which has made all Flexible Robot Caterpillars (FRC) go berserk and overrun cities which has left them uninhabitable except for a few aggressive alien species. FRC's are nuclear powered and were originally produced to transport huge amounts of cargo and people but was later used for military purposes.

You have been chosen to recapture the Capital City by destroying the FRC's in a tank over three levels with the ultimate aim to destroy the city which will remove the aliens so it can be rebuilt. The game is viewed from above with the screen showing a small part of the level which scrolls in various directions as you move. There are eight FRC's on a level and in their heads their carry fuel rods which are indestructible but the tails can be destroyed by blasting it with your laser. Once the tail has been destroyed you can collect the fuel rod which automatically appears in the nuclear reactor. Once all eight rods are in the reactor it is destroyed and you move to the next level. As well as the FRC's you must avoid or shoot the alien species that have made their home there.

To help you in your mission you are equipped with a laser as well as smart-bombs, heat seeking missiles and a shield. The laser's power is limited and when empty will only stun the aliens but can still destroy the tails of the FRC's. More laser power can be collected as well as your other weapons and shield, and are placed behind walls which can be destroyed, even with limited laser power. Your other weapons will destroy the aliens but will not destroy any FRC's tails. If you are touched by a FRC or an alien then you lose part of your shield and if your shield has gone then you need to get out of the tank by an escape pod. You have three tanks to complete your mission but if you are touched with no shield then it is game over.

171518.overview:
Lifeboat Adventure is a text adventure where the game claims to be based on a true story about the clipper Alana which hit a submerged reef of the north east coast and sank leaving just five survivors from 82 on August 10th 1927. You play the role of one of the survivors sat in a Lifeboat with four other people, Jake, Pedro, Shamus and a woman. You must interact with the other people as well as try to get the boat safely to land while trying to stay alive. The screen has text which describes your location and you type in commands with the keyboard to interact with your surroundings. 
Also released as part of "The Lockerby Collection".

171520.overview:
Lifeboat, also known as Lifeboat: A Waterlogged Adventure, is a text adventure that tests your seafaring skills for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Anthony Mario and published in Commodore Magazine 1989/04, as well as in Loadstar #059. 

Lifeboat is a small interactive adventure game which has most of the features you're accustomed to in text games. You use verb-noun commands like "Go House' or "Take box". If you want a two word noun, such as oil can take the second word, eg. "Take Can". Common text adventure abbreviations like N,S,E and W work instead of the full directions and U and D for up and down also work. Now you just need to figure out if you are on an ocean liner or a spacecraft.

171522.overview:
Life is a computerized version of Conway's Game of Life. It was developed by Cyndie Merten and published in Commodore Microcomputers Magazine 1985/06, and also released as part of Loadstar #012. Life simulates the growth and decay cycle of organisms. Processes like this are done to predict the growth of bacteria and the like in laboratory experiments. The concept was developed by John Horton Conway at the University of Cambridge. The rules are simple: 
 
1. Any organism surrounded by two or 3 neighbors survives. 
2. Four or more neighbors spells death for an organism due to overpopulation. 
3. No neighbors or only one also spells death due to isolation. 
4. An empty cell with exactly 3 neighbors will have an organism born into it.  
 
There are two versions of the game included. The first version creates random starting patterns. The other allows  you to set the pattern. Press the * to place a cell. Press the space bar to erase the cell. Press return to begin the lifecycle.

171523.overview: The Game of Life, also known simply as Life, is a cellular automaton, originally devised by the British mathematician John Horton Conway in 1970.  The game is a zero-player game, meaning that its evolution is determined by its initial state, requiring no further input. One interacts with the Game of Life by creating an initial configuration and observing how it evolves. Published in 64'er 1986/01.

171527.overview: A game based on Conway's game of life and published in SYS PD Diskett#30 (1992), and in Digital Marketing PD #088. The game of life is a cellular automaton created by John Horton Conway. A cellular automaton is a set of cells represented in a grid which can evolve through time thanks to basic rules.

171529.overview: The year is 2197. All life on Platar has been wiped out. Cause: Alien infiltration. Your mission is to find the aliens and if hostile, to destroy them. You are on the mother ship. through a viewing window you can see the base Amigar. There is a teleporter here. What next...?

171532.overview:
Published in the type-in book, "BASIC Computer Games - Microcomputer Edition". The game of Life was originally described in Scientific American  magazine, October, 1970. The computerized version of LIFE can be found on many computer systems--in many cases with Teletype print routines.  This version allows initial patterns to be composed directly on-screen and instant visualization of each generation as it is created.  In addition,patterns may be stored and recalled from seven memory pattern registers.  The generation speed may be controlled from the console. 
 
A.Genetic Rules
Cells (organisms, ducks, people, plants, etc.) reproduce, exist or die according to certain genetic laws.  Conway derived the genetic law of the game of LIFE from the following criteria:1.  There should be no initial patterns for which there is a simple proof that the population can grow without limit.2.  There should be initial patterns that apparently do grow without limit.3.  There should be simple initial patterns that grow and change for a considerable period of time before coming to an end in one of three possible ways:
a.  fading away completely (no life)
b.  becoming stable (no change in pattern or population)
c.  a pattern oscillates in an endless cycle of two or more periods.
Think of each cell as being a square of a checkerboard.  A celI may be either empty (shownas a space [no *] on the screen and in the following examples) or living (shown as an * bothon the screen and in the examples).  In the following examples, a '+' indicates an empty cell which is becoming a living cell.

171533.overview:
A strategy game set in the bizarre world of cellular automata and published in Commodore Disk User 1989/01-02. Life is a mathematical game devised by the Cambridge mathematician John Horton Conway. Following its introduction by Martin Gardner in Scientific American in 1970 it swept the computing world. Having encountered various Basic versions and finding them to be crude, slow and difficult to use I decided to write my own 'deluxe'
The rules of Life. 

In its pure form. Life is played on an infinite grid this is reduced in my version to 40x24. Each grid point can either contain a cell or be empty. The object of the game is to set up an Initial configuration of cells on the grid and then apply Conway's genetic laws' for births, deaths and survivals. These laws were carefully chosen to make the behavior of the population of cells both interesting and unpredictable

To understand the rules, note that each grid point is surrounded by eight neighboring points. The rules are:
* Survivals. Each cell with two or three neighbors survives.
* Deaths. Any cell with four or more neighbors dies of overcrowding. Any cell with one or no neighbors dies of isolation
* Births. A new cell will be born in each empty point surrounded by exactly three cells.
All births and deaths occur simultaneously and constitute a single generation in the life of a configuration.

171534.overview:
An implementation of John Conway's game of life as published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1995/01, a disk-only release.

Conway's Game of Life is a cellular automaton that is played on a 2D square grid. Each square (or "cell") on the grid can be either alive or dead, and they evolve according to the following rules:

    Any live cell with fewer than two live neighbors dies (referred to as underpopulation).
    Any live cell with more than three live neighbors dies (referred to as overpopulation).
    Any live cell with two or three live neighbors lives, unchanged, to the next generation.
    Any dead cell with exactly three live neighbors comes to life.

The initial configuration of cells can be created by a human, but all generations thereafter are completely determined by the above rules. The goal of the game is to find patterns that evolve in interesting ways – something that people have now been doing for over 50 years.

171535.overview: A one player Tron\Light cycles\Snake style game.

171536.overview: Light-waves is a production of the Children's Television Workshop that provides adventures in thinking through worlds you create! Create and control your own energy networks, explore and experiment with the system and guide Light-riders to the source!

171537.overview:
Lions of the Universe is a side-scrolling shoot 'em up set in space, with a feel resembling Armalyte in many ways. Players battle through a mazey territory, collecting tokens (which are left in the open, rather than collected form shot enemies) to improve weaponry. Enemies come towards you in waves and individually. Published in Game On 1994/01.

A planned sequel called Return of the Lions was in the works, but never finished/released. There is a playable demo version of that game, however.

171538.overview: You find yourself inside a refueling-sphere. The only thing you remember is that you are a robot, and that there has been a power failure. The sphere has no obvious exits....what now?

171539.overview: Guide the little guy to collect pieces of a puzzle, but don't touch anything else or you die. It's hard and it makes my senses ache. An action game published in 64'er Sonderheft 1985/03.

171540.overview: A slick looking Tron Light-Cycles style game for one player.

171541.overview: A two player only, Tron\Lightcycles style game published in the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 1999 (C64CGC).

171542.overview: Lights On is a puzzle game in which the objective is to light all the tiles on each of the 24 single-screen levels. Using a joystick, you control a character that moves around the grid of tiles lighting each tile it touches, and landing on a tile that's already lit turns it off again. Some levels take advantage of this mechanic, requiring you to move back and forth over tiles several times to turn them all on. Also scattered around the grid are arrow tiles that push your character in the indicated direction and teleporters can be used to instantly move to another corresponding tile. But we warned, this isn't a leisurely stroll of reckless lighting; a timer counts down at the start of each level. If you run out run of time you lose one of your five lives. Fortunately, some levels include a tile that add seconds to the timer - and you will need it, as there isn't much room for error.

171543.overview: Linking Leroy Visits LEGOLAND is an unreleased video game for Commodore 64 developed by Fairlight. The game is a 2D platformer, with two levels, one based on Town and the other Classic Space. Work on the game started in 1991, and a preview was released in 1992 as part of Fairlight's "LEGOLAND 2" demo. The game came between scenes of the demo, linking them together, leading to the game's name. Fairlight's connections with LEGO were later broken, and while the game's developers initially planned on removing the LEGO graphics and finishing it, the project was eventually abandoned.

171544.overview: A scrolling screen platformer published in Golden Disk 64 #04 (1989). Jump through the level and collect the stars while avoiding the Owlbats, Bee, Saucers and other and other monsters.

171553.overview:
Starlight #3. Find the keys to the doors and make your way out of the maze of twisty passages. 
 
You have been offered a wonderful job opportunity that you absolutely do not want to miss. But unfortunately, your arch enemy, having learned of the situation, has decided to prevent you from reaching your appointment on time. He tricked you into a spinning shuttle and locked you up in a maze. The only way to defeat your enemy will be to wander around your prison and try to reach the way out. Collect the keys to open the various doors and beware that some walls are illusory. But also remember that traps of various kinds are sown almost everywhere: some deadly, others to carry you from one part of the labyrinth to the other. Good luck! 
 
Published as Minotaurus in Italy's Videoteca Computer n.4.

171554.overview: This was originally a simple game that could be loaded up into memory while your Mastertronic full game was loading. This was intended to give you a mini-game to play while your purchased game was loading. the game was present on a number of Bulldog (Mastertronic) games such as Street Beat.

171555.overview: You must do all the things at once! This is shown as a single player game, but both joysticks should be used as one set moves you and allows you to switch tracks to avoid oncoming trains and avoid bombs dropped by the planes while the other shoots smoke and steam to allow you to better avoid those hazards. All this while keeping an eye on the track layout below to get where you need to and keep fueled up. Perhaps two players playing cooperatively would be most successful.

171556.overview:
Locomotion is a flick screen game where you take control of a locomotive from the Wild West days to collect trucks of gold to deliver to the bank. The game has two modes and they are Adventure or Arcade and both have four difficulty levels. In Adventure you are able to speed up or slow down the locomotive along the tracks and also control the points of the track ahead to change to new tracks. As you explore the area you will encounter trucks and these contain various items as well as gold and these include livestock, fuel and a sheriff. To hook up to a truck, you must reverse at 20mph or less and you automatically pick the truck up. You can also unhook any trucks when you stop.

On some sections of the track are broken parts and you need to unhook the right truck next to the broken part to repair it. Bandits from Mexico are in the area and if you stop next to them for a few seconds then they steal your gold unless you have a truck with a sheriff in it. Runaway trains roam the tracks driven by the ghosts of previous drivers looking to keep the gold. To keep the train moving you need to keep your fuel and water levels up by stopping at fuel dumps or water towers. If you crash, hit a ghost train or run out of fuel or water then you lose one of five lives.

In Arcade mode you have no control of the speed of the locomotive and you have to survive for as long as possible by changing the points to move on to new tracks. If you crash then it is game over.

171558.overview: A Frogger style game, cross the busy thoroughfare and the log filled river hazards to get to an unoccupied home.

171577.overview:
A take on Donkey Kong that was published in the book "Getting Ahead: Fantastic Games". You are a lumberjack who has just had his axe stolen by a bird. You must get to the bird by jumping logs and climbing ladders. Jump up to pull the ladders down. Get bonus points and an extra man every 8000 points. D to climb, Z is left, C is right and space bar to jump.

The game is a take on a rather infamous arcade Donkey Kong knockoff of the same name.

171578.overview:
Published in Commodore Disk User 1989/01-02. You don't have to be Mr Spock to solve this challenge to your intellect. It could help though... 
Logic is a game that careful thought. The computer will present you with an array of five pegs, each of which can be any one of five colors: red, green, yellow, blue and purple. The problem is that you don't know what colors are used or where they go. Don't despair, because the program will give you a number of tries It will tell you each time how many pegs you have got of the right color in the right place Dy displaying one to four black blocks, plus white blocks to show how many are the right color but are in the wrong place.  
 

The menu allows you a options when playing Logic. Besides the five color bars which allow you to place pegs, you can delete the last peg placed by choosing delete, i confirm your choice of pegs by entering Enter. The joystick is used to make all choices.

171580.overview:
A game by Piotr Malisiewicz and published in Magic Disk 64 1995/10. Concentration is required here when it comes to recreating the right square exactly and under time pressure. On the right side of the screen you can see the template. This is how your Quadrat (on the left) should look like at the end, and since it isn't like this when the game starts, it's time to roll up your sleeves and let's go. With a joystick in port 2 you can steer the small arrow horizontally and vertically back and forth between the four columns of your square. At the push of a button, the row to which the arrow is pointing is shifted by one position. You must now try to move the rows as cleverly as possible so that the entire square resembles the example on the right.
Since the whole move is also subject to a strict time limit, you don't have much time to ponder and think. Another tip: to get the arrow from the horizontal to the vertical, you have to move it all the way to the right on the top and simply press the joystick down. The arrow then switches automatically. Have fun!

171581.overview: A peculiarly perplexing and potentially punishing Polish puzzle pastime.

171582.overview: Stretch your brain and decode the symbols.

171583.overview: A logic based puzzle game created by Jacques Lebbe and published in 1983 by Micro Application.

171585.overview: A text adventure that uses selectable answers to navigate the game in which you are a Texas ranger and must don a mask to catch the villians.

171589.overview:
Long Lance: A Computer Game of Tactical Naval Combat in the South Pacific is a strategic naval simulation of Japanese and American forces in the South Pacific during World War II.

Designed for 1 - 2 players, each player controls either the American or Japanese forces. A computer opponent is available for 1-player games. The viewpoint is of the theater naval commander, and the player composes task forces, establishes missions and destinations for those groups, and responds to operational events.

The game is text-only, and came with a board and physical pieces to allow the player to keep track of the location of theirs and enemy units. Gameplay includes Savo Island on 9 August 1942, Cape Esperance on 11 October, Guadalcanal on 13 November, Guadalcanal on 14 November, and Tassafaronga on 30 November. Time passes in 20 minute intervals, allowing the player to input new commands for their fleet, but will stop to allow the player to react to enemy movements. Gameplay consists of nighttime battles, and each scenario begins at 1800 and ends at 0600 the next morning.

During each gameplay segment, the player sets taskforce management, where the player can combine and split ships from each group to create new groups. The player also sets movement orders for their ships. The player adjusts battle doctrine for each group, including open/close range rules, rules of engagement, and tactical guidance. The player's vessels then follow their commanding officer's directions for a 20 minute interval, at which point they await new orders.

171590.overview:
A multi-genre package that contains both "Old MacDonald's Farm" and "SORT - Space Observer Recruitment Test" games. 
The "Old MacDonald's Farm" game consists of 3 sections: Memory, Observation and Reflections. 

In Memory a friendly farmer will show you a puzzle consisting of 4 animals from his farm with information for each, after a few seconds the labels will disappear and you will have to put them back in their proper place. 

In Observation you will be presented by MacDonald with 3 apparently identical sequences but only 2 are identical. Spot the difference. 

In Reflections you will be shown two images that are continuously changing but they will be the same for a brief period. Hit the button when they match!

Released as Chiribiduf in Italy in Videoteca Computer (EV) n.10.

171595.overview:
The first clue as to the unconventional nature of this text adventure is the scant description within the game manual. Unlike most games of its era, Lords of Karma doesn't rely on a written narrative peppered with enticing illustrations to prepare and color the player's experience. Even Lords of Karma's plot is to be discovered in-game, just like the vistas and scents of its magical world. There is treasure, of course, and deadly foes, but what to do with the spoils of adventure? You only know that you quest for "karma points" to take to heaven, and that you begin in the central square of the mythical city of Golconda.

The standard abbreviations and two-word commands move you through this text-only, turn-based adventure, but don't stand there gawking. While looking twice can reveal something missed the first time, it will also put you in the maw of a hungry crocodile. Happily, rebirth is just around the corner. Dying doesn't end your game -- the karmic wheel keeps turning. It simply strips you of your worldly goods and puts you on a mountaintop. The map is fixed, and the karma points are yours to keep, so progress belongs to the persistent (and those who find the in-game hint book).

171603.overview: Welcome to the search for Dutchman's GOLD. I'm the ghost of backpack Sam, yer guide for this adventure. It's very dangerous and I hope that you don't end up a ghost like me! Deep in the Superstition Mountains of Arizona, hidden in the eerie mists of forgotten times, the Lost Dutchman's Gold Mine awaits the fortune-seeker bold enough to challenge the fates. Protected by bands of hostile Indians, the ravines and gullies harbor silent death for the unwary adventurer. You start in a miner's shack in the desert below the mountains with a mule, a rifle, and a few tools. There is a map hidden somewhere and this is your clue to uncountable wealth. There is a ghost town, and the desert, and, ultimately, the deadly Superstitions to explore as you search for the way to the Lost Dutchman's Mine.

171606.overview:
A multiscreen platform shooter created by Sven Forstmann and published in 64'er Sonderheft 85. The struggle to return home. Lost in a strange world. Search the interplanetary outbacks lonely robot returning home. Control him. Find the way out for him. But watch out for attackers. 
 
An interesting experiment was on the agenda. Until now, the only way to traverse hyperspace was in space gliders. For the first time in human history, a new transmitter should make it possible to jump through the universe - without costly take-offs and landings, without time differences and without the long journey in a spaceship. One quick step through the dimensional gate of the transmitter - and the journey would be over. But before the first human beings were sent on their journey, this new achievement had to be tested. With a humanoid, a robot. Only his notes could provide information about the dangers of a dimensional journey.

Today, February 20th, 4003, the time has come. The antennas of the transmitter are aimed at a planet in the constellation  of Alpha Centaur. A 16LXY23 type robot is sent. The settings are only off by a millionth of a degree, but where did he end up and can he get home!

171607.overview: Lost Tomb takes the player into the depths of an ancient pyramid, though its location is uncertain (the box covers of the home versions place it in Egypt, but in-game it is said to be deep in the Amazon). To escape, you will need to make your way from chamber to chamber - uncovering treasures, avoiding traps, and facing a variety of enemies from scorpions and spiders to mummies and gigantic bats. Like every self-respecting explorer and treasure-hunter, you've armed yourself with a gun and a whip: the whip clears away everything in your immediate vicinity - enemies, traps and even walls. Your gun can be infinitely reloaded, but whips are limited (though you can restock along the way). The pyramid itself dislikes your presence: if you loiter too long, or step onto a trap, the earth will shake and the walls will shoot! Alongside the treasure chambers, each level of the pyramid has a stairway which takes you deeper down, with two different exits; fortunately, you're equipped with a map to help you plan your route. Beware the special throne rooms, rarely encountered and chock-full of traps.

171608.overview: You are Edward Malone, a reporter for the Daily Gazette. Dispatches you have been getting from your friend Maple White have stopped coming. Maple had been describing a lost world he had discovered. Thinking the worst you set out for this world. Arriving at the base camp below plateau cliffs you discover that Maple has died. You want to find out how he died and also explore this strange land. Just how to get to the top of the cliffs? The Lost World is a text adventure with no graphics. On the screen you can read about your surroundings as well as type in commands to discover progress on your adventure.

171609.overview: A puzzle game created by Méhész Levente, with music by Sándor Fodor of the group Thunders and released as a public domain game in 1995.

171610.overview: An adult game of forfeits and rewards intended for 2 players. The naughtiest thing your CBM64 ever did! Over 13000 possible combinations, you may get tired from playing it, but you'll never get tired of it!

171611.overview: A sexually themed Quiz\Party game for up to 18. Though contestants may want to be at least 18... years of age. Interactive Fantasy game for two or more intimate players. Amusing and suggestive trivia. Quiz format with provocative "scoring" system.

171612.overview: Love quest allows a people, or group of people to answer a string of questions to learn facts about themselves and create a compatibility profile and match them with other people who have used the game.

171613.overview: In Love Tramp you hurdle fences, jump over spiders and avoid the crows on the way to reunite with... Trampette? It might be true love if you can just save her. Game does not contain Smurf Sex.

171615.overview: Lucky Egg is a multi-screen platformer game, published by ArtGame, which was released in 1995.

171616.overview:
You are the pilot of a spacecraft flying over the surface of an alien planet when you realise your fuel is low and an emergency landing is needed. Problem is, the only place to land is a city so the solution is to bomb all the buildings to make a landing strip. The game is viewed from the side on a single screen where you fly from left to right, and when you reach the edge of the screen, you appear one place lower on the left side. You must drop bombs from your craft to remove each building and there a short delay between dropping bombs. If you remove the city then you move to the next level but if you hit a building then it is game over. 
 
Originally released by the developers for free in 1993 on the csdb, and later published in Commodore Zone Issue #01 (September 1995)

171617.overview: The player must try to land a lunar landing module on the moon keeping in account fuel, velocity and distance to the surface. Published as a game of the "Cassette 50" collection and also in Digital Marketing PD #234.

171618.overview: The player must try to land a lunar landing module on the moon keeping in account fuel, velocity and distance to the surface. This version has some good Skramble style graphics, one of the best versions graphically.

171619.overview: A lander style game. Aim to land on the green pad. Joystick down to leave the ship, joystick up to stop the ship. Created by L. Smithdale and published in 1983.

171620.overview:
A Uridium style shooter. Man's adventure in space requires a series of tools that can allow survival in a hostile environment or in any case, unsuitable for normal human functions. The problem of the lack of the force of gravity can skew both physical and mental equilibrium. The danger of exposure to cosmic rays, extreme and fluctuating temperatures and lack of gasses necessary for breathing along with the normal hardships and difficulties that arise create the need for a protective shell within which we can recreate the environmental conditions existing on Earth. All this to allow men and women to carry out the work of the day. This led to the creation of the spacecraft: a vehicle that is sturdy, thermally insulated, and can maneuver to allow travel in space. Equipped with rocket engines controlled by the human pilots in a manner similar to aircraft. Every system must be reliable and redundant to ensure that a small inconvenience doesn't turn the crew into a bright red stain. Unfortunately, in the course of human events, one of these ships must wage war against another, and take on the defenses of a large space station in the process, so grab the controls safe in the knowledge that your incredibly advanced ship was created by the lowest military bidder and hope there are no brightly colored inconveniences in your future. 

Published as L.E.M. in Italy in Videoteca Computer n.4.

171621.overview:
Welcome to the magical and criminal atmosphere of Lupenio. In this game, Lupenio the greatest thief of all time decides to realize his dream: to steal the wonderful diamond of King Solomon, hidden in a room of an ancient house full of dangerous guardians and deadly traps.

Be careful my friend and remember... every key opens one and only one door so pay attention and try to find the right strategy.
Published in New Special Playgames N°09 (Maggio 1988) supplement: Games Commodore 64 N°1.

171622.overview: The Lüsher Profile lets you look into your mind and personality by analyzing your preferences for various colors, shades and shapes. By recording and interpreting your responses to a variety of tests, a profile emerges of the factors which define your current approach to work, to relationships and to life in general.

172585.overview:
A Space Invader/Gorf style shooter where you are at Carnival but one where every joke counts. The aliens have camouflaged themselves as smiling masks, but underneath they are grim death dealing machines. They must be shot down mercilessly and not allowed to have the last laugh. Beware, they come from all directions, even below. 

Published in Italy as Le Machere in Supplementi Sipe - i Magnifici 10 (Settembre 1984).

173057.overview: An educational  math game for children that teaches them and tests them on their addition and subtraction skills.  Developed and published by Learning Technologies, Inc. in 1985. For kids Pre-Kindergarten to third grade.

173075.overview: An evil army of enemy space soldiers has invaded a space station. The player, taking the role of the infamous fictional character Lee Enfield, must recover the control of the base, locating and destroying all the enemies. Space Ace is a multi-directional scrolling shooter game also known as a crosshairs shooter where the player must shoot each enemy soldier in a limited amount of time, before that the enemy soldier shoots the player.

173754.overview: Los Templos Sagrados is a Spanish text-adventure, the sequel to La Diosa de Cozumel, and the second "book" of the "Ci-U-Than" trilogy of games. They all utilize the parser DAAD, that has capabilities similar to the Infocom Z-machine one (you can chain commands, correct misspellings, etc). This time around the player searches the ruins of the Yucatán peninsula for the lost Mayan temple of Chichén Itzá.

173980.overview: Do you like word games? Then you'll love Up for Grabs. Because it's fast paced, exciting and educational all at the same time. You've got to think fast. Because you have to grab the letters you want off the rotating cube before anyone else does. Then you'll need to place them in your playing area and build words as quickly as you can! But don't go so quickly that you aren't able to plan ahead. Those gray squares are double word scores and letters that don't make words count against you.

174304.overview: Power Box Leicester & Stafford, Morning and Afternoon Shift. Set on a Summer day in the mid 1980's the simulation allows you to control traffic for two four hour shifts which we think you will find challenging as you keep traffic flowing smoothly with the minimum of delay to booked timings.

174427.overview:
In 1988 Lode Runner was re-released with 192 new levels of play by Artis Software. While it still contained the original release's Broderbund title screen it also added one from Artis. 

The Bungeling Empire has stolen a huge cache of gold from its rightful owners, and your mission is to infiltrate its treasury and recapture it. This entails progressing through 150 screens of platforms, ladders and ropes.

The Empire has sent robotic guards down to protect the gold, and contact with any of these will cost you a life. Your method of escaping them is to press fire to dig a hole in their line of movement, thus causing them to fall in briefly, allowing you to move across the gap safely. Once all the gold has been collected, a ladder allowing you to move onto the next screen is added. Completing these screens often requires forward planning and precision.

This was one of the earliest games to include a level editor, allowing the creation of new level designs with no programming skill.

174656.overview: Lode Runner II (disk version) is an almost 1:1 copy of Lode Runner, but with 104 completely new fan-created levels (from 4711-Soft). The colour of the bricks was changed from red to blue. Take note that there is also a defect image of this version on the internet, with only 21 playable levels - the levels 22 upwards were overwritten with other data.

174659.overview:
Lode Runner IV (disk version) also a fan edit, with bright green bricks. From the 127 levels only 32 are new, the other 95 are copies from Lode Runner II, partially in a different order.   
 
A messenger arrived at dawn and brought the news that the precious Egyptian statues, found during the excavations of Giza had been stolen by the insane collector Goldstar who locked them in blocks of graphite and kept them in the hall of his crazy museum. To recover the precious treasure and overcome the assiduous vigilance of the dangerous guardians of the museum, Professor Jones decided to read the papyri of Set, able to give him the power of temporary transmutation of matter. Armed with this ability, he will have to recover the entire haul by misleading the guards with skillful maneuvers and using that power to generate unpredictable pitfalls in the stone to trap or waylay them. 

Published in Italy as Trafugator in I Magnifici 5 & 7 n.23 (aprile 1987), Hit Parade C64 n.15 (Settembre 1987), and Hit Parade C64 n.64 (Febbraio 1992).

174660.overview: Lode Runner V (disk version) another fan edit, with blue bricks. From the 107 levels even only 14 are new, the other are copies (partially from Lode Runner II and IV).

174661.overview: Loderunner Mix, also known as Hansmanns Lode Runner was created by DrHonz of Reengine & Mod. He has updated it again in 2010 and in 2016 calling that one the Tricky Mix which was a clean up version of the original project.

175932.overview:
Mine Canyon is an avoid-it game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John Krutch and published by Ion International, Inc. in Ahoy! 1986/09 (Issue #33).

The game is also known under the names Run Throught and Lauf Durch!

176901.overview:
Published in Keypunch's Adventure Quest IV compilation and as part of "The Big 100" collection of games. 

The king of Portugal believes there is a sea route to India; in this strategy games players need to find it! Players will need to deal with hunger, pirates, storms, unhappy crews, and more as they explore the open seas.

177446.overview: Published in both  Loadstar #010, and in the Best of Loadstar #2, this text adventure by Rod Rudd was originally created for the Apple II and later ported to the C64. You must fight the legions of the dead and destroy the necromancer.

177472.overview: In this short (only three levels) but fun platformer (which also has some puzzle elements) your goal is to take all the rivets from the platforms before the time runs out (not as simple as it looks). The end level also involves rescuing a girl. Developed by Roland Kunz and published by BB Software.

178331.overview:
Gone with the Wind (Via Col Vento) is appropriate as for all creatures you face, a single shot is enough! You have five lives to sustain you, the war is nearly over, but you have to keep going and have only your courage by your side as you wander in the endless caves using your survival skills to keep you safe from the pitfalls of nature. This immense clay cave full of burial niches, tunnels, crumbling stairs and terrifying creatures is proof the war has not ended for you. But fate is not completely against you because in the cave, scattered here and there are various types of weapons and some creatures require a certain type of weapon to best destroy. 

Published in Italy under Via Col Vento in  Linguaggio Macchina C64/ZX n.14 (Febbraio 1986) and as L'Errante in Poke n.10 (febbraio 1986).

178375.overview: Lernaia is a rare Greek language shooter for the C64. It was developed by Sotos Demetriou in 1984. Shoot the monsters with your torch until you face the end boss.

178410.overview:
La Geste d'Artillac is an Adventure game, developed and published by Infogrames.

Your father has been kidnapped and his house burnt to the ground. You pick a few items and try to find him in a strange and deserted land.

178420.overview:
Des Chiffres et des Lettres ("Numbers and Letters") is a French game show which inspired the similar British programme Countdown. Two players compete in a sequence of rounds challenging language and arithmetic skills. In this version you can turn off either type of rounds, and can have infinite time to think in each round, if you wish.

In letters rounds, an array of 9 letters is chosen by each player alternately choosing either a vowel or a consonant, and players must find the longest possible legitimate word. In numbers rounds, an array of face-down numbers (including 25, 50, 75 and 100 as well as 2 each of 1-10) is presented to the player, who chooses the number of 'large' numbers. A target between 101 and 999 is then generated, and players must get as close to this as possible. Additionally, there are mental arithmetic challenge rounds, in which players must solve an equation as quickly as possible.

178422.overview:
A supercomputer in the most remote part of a distant galaxy has become crazy and threatens to destroy the planet. You have been chosen to be the central link of the support command which will try to give a solution for it. But don't worry, you have been educated and trained in the Golden Ring space station, the hardest survival school of the galactic confederation.

Besides, your ship is equipped with the ultimate devices which will allow you to travel safely by the well-known universe. The Combat Mode, where you can activate a panel with a system to locate and to destroy your enemies and the Control System via Menus, both make La Aventura Espacial a new concept in the graphic-conversational adventure.

First of all, your mission is to find your companions, whom are distributed by all the universe, and together with them you must arrive to the central base of the Dark Threat. There, you will have to deal one on one with the computer. It's not an easy task, but you are the last hope of the humanity. All the galaxy has its destiny in your hands.

178590.overview:
Live Ammo is a compilation of five games:

- Army Moves
- Green Beret
- Rambo: First Blood Part II
- The Great Escape
- Top Gun

178834.overview: This game is slightly different, compared to a lot of normal  shooters, and quite an original concept. Your mission is to approach an asteroid, and discover the source inside it. If you succeed with your mission, visit the author's web site shown on the end, followed by the code. This game can be played by 2 player team work - or alternatively, you can perhaps use two joysticks.

179003.overview:
Entered into the the Halloween Competition 2019 organized by "Phaze101, Commodore Creators, Commodore 64 Malta User Club and Facebook groups, in special collaboration with Double Sided Games".

You must guide Luna the witch through a never ending series of caves while avoiding and dispatching of enemies. As you progress Luna will fly faster and faster and the caves will get tighter and tighter. If you build up the power bar by killing enough spooky enemies you'll gain rapid fire for a short while. Destroy all enemies in a wave to receive a points bonus. How far can you get??!

179920.overview:
You are an empath. You can contact the dead and hear "echoes" of events long past. And, like all the empaths, as your father and grandfather were, you are restless and adventurous.
And that's why you find yourself sailing the ether with the family flying boat, investigating one of the most dangerous Ghost Zones, where the cataclysms that shaped the world took place.
What you will discover in an old abandoned house will shed a very sinister light on the origin of everything ...

English translation by Pablo Martínez Merino and Gareth Pitchford.

179992.overview: Lala wanted to be a witch by all means, so she entered the Great Witch Academy, led by Mistress Morgana la Marrana, who admitted her ‘cause she didn’t have any pupils because of the worldwide crisis. Morgana herself taught the very first basics of magic and sorcery to Lala, who was not a very good student. One day, Morgana ran out of chipped man bile, so she went to the supermarket to buy some and Lala had to stay on her own in the academy with all those machines and magic filters to her disposal. She began trying some spells, and as nothing happened, she just opened the windows so to freshen the air. But before she could be aware, all the pots with magical filters and chemicals flew off  thru’ the window scattering all around the surroundings.

179997.overview: Lode Runner 250 Level Tricky Mix (Lode Runner X). The final incarnation of the 250 level challenge that has been reworked several times over the years. V1 released in 2010 and V2 in 2016. Do be patient, this will take a while to load even when in emulation.

180110.overview:
An updated basic version of the Arcade Lander game and published in Commodore Computing International v07-03 (Nov 1988).
- Single player 
- Joystick Port 2 
- 3 Levels

180137.overview: Just another mindless hero in a spacesuit. Laser damage increases every four levels. Deactivate the lasers, manage your thrusters and your shields to safely make your way to the next level. Published in Loadstar #163 and Loadstar #200.

180138.overview: A sequel to the original 1998 game. Manage your thrust and shields, the laser defense grid gets stronger every few levels. Make your way through the labyrinth and to the next level. Published in Loadstar #175, and republished in Loadstar #200.

180140.overview: You are an alien who just found a nice uninhabited planet to colonize...or so you thought. This planet is very inhabited, and the natives don't like aliens just dropping in. Defend yourself! And get away from the planet as soon as possible.

180141.overview:
Originally intended to be updated monthly this is an educational quiz where you can flex your general knowledge. 

Developed by Jeffrey L Jones, and published in Loadstar #043.

180142.overview: 23 medium challenge Lode Runner levels released as a response to Conrad's very challenging levels for Lode Runner.

180143.overview: 150 very challenging Lode Runner levels published in Loadstar #190. According to Loadstar #190 these levels were created by Fred, Barbra and Nicole Conrad, the team, from Burnaby, British Columbia that has created more levels than any other group, over 750 levels at the time up this game's publication. Some controls for the game are: CTRL-R to quit the level, CRL-U to go up a level, CTRL-F to add extra lives and CTRL-Z to disable the iris effect. CTRL-A to abort the current life if you get stuck and CRTL-E to go to the Edit screen. The first level requires you to perform an advanced trick to solve. You have to ride on top of a bad guy as he falls, jumping off at just the right point to pick up a gold bar that is otherwise impossible to get. It continues to be this challenging throughout. Good luck!

180591.overview: An early update to Lode Runner prior to the CSDb plus system that added a menu of choices as to the levels to run you would like to run. Choices were the original Professional Loderunner 1-75 levels, Professional Loderunner 2 and the 76-150 levels there, Loderunner Championship, Loderunner 5 and Loadrunner Classic.

180592.overview: A compilation of other Lode Runner levels, presented without much in the way of acclaim or fanfare for the people who compiled them, but considered a unique game entry and a snapshot of the times.

180652.overview: A 2 player only game of Tron Cycles published in 64 Tape Computing No. 03 (1984/08-09). Duel to the death on the games grid!

180901.overview:
A typing education game where you move your Sumo wrestler forward by typing the correct letters as quickly as possible.

Published in Italy as Lotta Sumo in Formula 64 n.5 and Play on tape Nuova serie - Sport Simulator 3.

181519.overview:
An arcade style collect'em up game. The Pennysland thermonuclear power plant was attacked by a group of rebels who want to bring the government forces to their knees, depriving the whole region of vital energy. The rebels then sabotaged some power lines to prevent the power plant from coming back into operation. Moving with your vehicle, hanging from the energy grid, you must attempt to restore all damaged contacts, but beware your enemies are lurking and will try to attack you to prevent you from completing your task. If you have finished one sector you will be able to move on to the next one, but it appears to be a little more difficult. 

Published in Italy as Loop in Hit Parade C64 n.38 (Ottobre 1989) and in New Special PlayGames n.21 (giugno 1989).

181942.overview: A very unofficial sequel to Lode Runner II with some minor changes.

182099.overview:
The most basic of games. Find your way out of the maze but with a gravity-like twist, from the book "The Commodore 64 Games Book - 21 Sensational Games", which was published in German as "Das Commodore 64 Spiele-Buch - 21 raffinierte Spiele", in Finnish as "Commodore 64 Ohjelmoinnin opas - Pelit", and in Italian as "Il Libro dei Giochi del Commodore 64,"

Steer the ball through the maze from beginning to end, without letting it drop into one of the holes. It needs a steady hand and quick reactions but given a little practice it can be done. Controls use Z, X, ; and /.

183187.overview:
Gold Grabber (also called Lode Runner Jr.) is a single-screen platformer developed by Andrew S. Pakerski and published in 1986 by Softalk Production in Loadstar #20. 

There are only about 6 screens in total, however, every time you complete all screens, the screens just repeat and increase in speed every time you have to repeat each screen, so the disappearing platforms speed up every time you play each screen, which makes the game a bit more challenging.

184881.overview:
Verkeers Rally is an educational game in which the player has to look for control stations in a busy and unknown metropolis to reach the finish through the knowledge of map reading and traffic rules. But the player must locate six transmitters within one hour. However, each transmitter contains a battery that only works for ten minutes. The first transmitter works from 9:50 to 10:00. The second from 10:00 to 101.0 etc. until at 10:50 the sixth transmitter battery is exhausted and the game is over. With these means the player can find the transmitters:

Large blue signs with white letters on which "Signal" is displayed; These indicate an electronic arrow in the direction of the currently working transmitter.
District map: when the player parks there and presses the fire button, you get to see the part of the city where you are at that moment. A green rectangle represents the entire city; a small gray rectangle indicates in which part you are now. A small white dot is the first transmitter.
Sonar stations: if the player parks here, you will see the part of the town where you are at that moment and hear a whistle and see white dots on the screen. The faster they go, the closer you are to the transmitter.

The buildings with the inscription "Puzzle": if the player parks here and presses the fire button, you will see a part of the city where the transmitter is located. By means of the map that you find in the manual, you can find out which part of the city that is. From the third channel (from 10:20 onward) only pieces of the plan are shown. During the search for the transmitters, the game is interrupted regularly to ask the player about certain traffic situations, such as identifying which of the road users has priority. The player also has to refuel regularly at one of the filling stations. Because if the player is without petrol, there will be an automatic refuel and the player will pay penalty seconds. So the player must keep an eye on the fuel gauge at the bottom of the screen. If the player sees a black rectangle appear on the pavement, the player must stop and press the fire button; one of the transmitters has been found.

188977.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter from Ian Jones & Michael Jones. The Interplanetary Federation has decided to make a raid on the Zynon-Lotec platform which a small group of rebels uses as a starting point to carry out their retaliatory actions. The plan is to land you on the platform about a mega-crawler. At this point you will have to penetrate into enemy territory and aim directly at the rebel headquarters. Of course, you won't find it easy. Many previous attempts, however, have allowed the rebels to gather information on the type of protection that the rebels have set up to defend their headquarters. As soon as you land you will be attacked by constant waves of enemy fighters. While you are defending yourself you will have to pay close attenton to where you move to avoid falling into the traps prepared to block you. Good luck!

190529.overview:
Jack Lockerby was one of the stars of early Commodore 64 gaming and here is a collection of some of his lesser known text adventure treasures. Game contains:
Hammer of Grimmold; Lifeboat; Realm of Darkness; The Mutant; Matchmaker; The Cup; Witch Hunt

192135.overview: Las Vegas a Gogo is a simple slot machine game coded in BASIC and published hy Addison-Wesley Publishers Ltd. in their 1984 book "Crazy Games for Your Commodore 64".

192300.overview: A combination of the multigenre games Lorella 1 and Lorella 2 games that were published in Alga Soft #10B with the payoff being pixilated nudes at the end of each of those sections. Also known as La Storia dei Sogni or La St. Dei Sogni on the tape cover.

192636.overview: The game introduces us to our character, who, invited by a friend of your father, challenges us to enter his own labyrinth in order to overcome his own test and escape from it alive. To do this, we place ourselves in a position on the map, already inside the labyrinth, from which we will only see the adjoining rooms (we recommend that you make a map) and we will advance. Along the way you will come across different aids or tests and you will have to overcome them, one by one, until you exit the maze.

194517.overview: Laser Legion is a shoot 'em up for 1 or 2 players (co-op) It was developed by Alf Yngve using Chris Yates' SEUCK engine and published by Binary Zone PD in 1989

195862.overview:
You are the lone survivor of an expedition to South America to find the famed Golden Condor. Your plane has crashed in the jungle and you are completely lost. 
 
Also contained in the trilogy release of "Harboro, Lost in the Amazon and St. Jives"

196123.overview:
A very different take on a Frogger\Freeway style game often called a single screen platformer, which makes sense because you can use each level as a platform and there are platform like sections to stand on. However the goal is to avoid being hit by the platforms and get to the very top of the screen. Once you choose your path you can only change your location by settling on a platform before proceeding upwards again from wherever the moving platforms take you.  
 
ARetroSytaxEra described it in verse, "Get on a block, into the groove, this is a crock, in mid-air you can't move."  
 
Published in Commodore 64 Club #02 [Italian Release].

196638.overview:
LOGO Mastermind is version of the popular logic game Mastermind, published in the C64 Magazine PowerPlay as a type-in tutor for LOGO.. 

You try to figure out a secret code made up of several unknown characters. You get to specify the number of characters in the code from two to six. You also get to set the number of possible letters that could be selected for any individual character in the code up to eleven. 

For example, if you set the code to five characters and the possible letters to nine, you would try to crack a code sequence like XXXXX where any of the X's could be one of the letters from A to I. 
 
IN addition to being published in Commodore Power/Play Vol.4 N.2 (April/May 1985), it was also published in Loadstar #011.

197390.overview: Lightraycer is a two player only Tron light cycles game. It was developed by Matthew Hall and released into the public domain. The year of release is unknown.

199296.overview: Lane X (also spelled as Lane 'X') is a pinball game made using Olaf Lubeck's PCS (PinballConstruction Set in 1992) The actual person(s) responsible for this particular PCS game are not known, however it was released on PCS Club Disk #28, which was circulated by a group that made public domain PCS games in the late 1980s-early 1990s.

199297.overview: Landung is a German language "lander" game developed by Karsten Neve and released into the public domain in 1985.

199302.overview: An adventure game full of humor and traps. Beware of gateways like guards!

199439.overview: The Folly of Gold. Looks like someone's attempt at making a H.E.R.O clone in BASIC. Equipped with a dorsal helicopter and a frontal laser, go to the end of your madness in some sinister settings with bad company. Published in both Hebdogiciel Hors Serie N°2, and Hebdogiciel Software N°1

199511.overview: Courageously oppose the childish pranks of a few terrorists in search of merry entertainment. A single screen platfomer created by Jean-Marc Daumont and published in Hebdogiciel Hors Serie N°2, and Hebdogiciel Software N°3.

199555.overview: Logitrumps is a card game, like we used to play it in the 80's similar to the card game "War". Each player (you and the computer) gets the same number of cards. Each card represents a retro computer and has several values like Year, memory, colors, RAM, etc. Each card has strength and weaknesses. If a computer has a lot of memory or colors, it usually isn't that old and therefor would likely lose in the year category. Usually the higher value wins with the exception of the year where the lower value wins. The player to win all the cards through strategic match-ups wins the game.

199556.overview: A compilation of games which includes "The Great Giana Sisters", "Gitty's Dreams 1\Gitty's Land", "Gitty's Dreams 2\Gitty's Revenge" & "Power-Sisters I", all with a live trainer and highscore save as a feature.

199607.overview: A set of 5 original Boulder Dash caves created by Lars Benhofen aka Schlonkel aka PST. The majority of the caves were created in the late 80's but were not released until this effort.

199608.overview: A set of 25 new Boulder Dash caves (20 caves and 5 intermissions) released by Lars Bernhofen aka Schlonkel of PST.

199610.overview: A set of 25 new Boulder Dash caves to explore and be puzzled by. Created by Lars Bernhofen (schlonkel) for PST using Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction kit as a launching point. Created using the CLCK 3.0 Engine with Hidden Cave code.

199611.overview: A new set of 25 Boulder Dash puzzle levels to explore. All created by Lars Bernhofen (schlonkel) based off the Boulder Dash Construction set by Pete Liepa, this specific set created with the Carzy Light Construction Kit version 3.0.

199612.overview: The golden ring of Boulder Dash games, created by Lars Bernhofen (schlonkel) and based on Peter Liepa's BDCK. Exploring the final frontier, 20 plus one new and challenging caves to outwit.

199621.overview: For a fistful of diamonds...get this new set of 24 Boulder Dash caves from Lars Bernhofen (schlonkel).

199622.overview: Where the caves have much fame. More diamond-hunting Boulder Dash goodness in the shape of 24 new caves (30 levels in total, some the creator considered "intermissions") from Lars Bernhofen (schlonkel). All caves created with CLCK V3.0 and the PLCK engine.

199623.overview: The Lost Caves 8 (Final) "In No Sense? Nonsense!" Over 30 new Boulder Dash caves to explore and overcome, released at Doreco-Party 2013/Doreco #38 by Lars Bernhofen (schlonkel).

202310.overview: Lost Realms of Murkasada: Episode 1 is a brand new freeware adventure game with role-playing elements  for the Commodore 64. It was released on June 16, 2021 and developed by Arkanix Labs. It is a companion/side adventure/rpg-lite of their development C64 CRPG Crimson Twilight which they are currently working on.

202677.overview:
Lady Pac is a maze game for the Commodore 64.

It is a homage to Ms. Pac-Man, an arcade game published by Midway in 1982.

Main differences from the original version:

•   Randomly generated mazes
•   Bonus rounds

The game works perfectly on both PAL and NTSC models. However, for game speeds similar to the original arcade game, it is suggested using an NTSC model.

204645.overview: Released in 1984, League Soccer is a mail-order only game by Sophisticated Games designed to simulate a soccer season. The player is able to configure a league with between 2 and 24 teams of their choice. Each team is given a rating between 1 and 9 which will affect their ability throughout the game and can be given a name of up to 8 characters. The main menu gives you several options and the first gives you the ability to simulate a week of the season. This will show you all of the games for that week and allow you to give a score out of 100 which will bias the chances of the home team. This will default to a value based on the ratings of the teams involved but can be adjusted if required.

206596.overview: Star Video Poker (also known as Loadstar's Video Poker) is a casino video poker game developed by John Serafino in 1996. It was published in Loadstar #142. Plays with Joystick (in port 1) or a Commodore mouse.

206637.overview:
An exciting word game with some twists, plus skill level options. For the Commodore 1 28, 64, Plus/4, and C16. Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/02 (Issue #32). Like a bowl of alphabet soup, the "Lexitron" screen appears to be just a jumbled mass of letters. Can you find the ten hidden words before time runs out? 
 
If you enjoy the hidden word games often found in newspapers and magazines, you'll like "Lexitron." But unlike the ones done with pencil and paper, Lexitron 
adds a few twists. There's 'a time limit, and you can select one of three difficulty levels.

206679.overview: A Worm\Snake game published in COMPUTE! 1984/04 (Issue #47) and in the Street Games "Red Box" release in Australia and New Zealand. The game is featuring Nerm the Worm, who is trapped in Bemer Castle and would like nothing more than to escape (and consume a generous helping of "magic mushrooms" along the way). Yet another variation on Snake where the player controls a serpentine crawler in perpetual motion, which must be guided to consume food, dodge deadly walls, and avoid biting its own tail. The castle is composed of eleven rooms, each trickier to navigate than the last. In a vaguely Carrollian manner, the rooms are prone to sprouting mushrooms which cause Nerm to grow as he eats them: after consuming five mushrooms, the exit doors will open, leading to the next room. Extra lives are awarded along the way, presumably another effect of the magical fungi.

207374.overview:
You control a lunar module attempting to successfully land on the moon's surface. Alternately, lower a capsule to a crash-free landing. Whatever it takes to get the points. In the First level, you must touch down on one of the landing pads in the mountains. You have the choice of landing at either the 500 point pad or the 100 point pad. Once you have landed at both pads, however, the 100 point pad disappears, leaving a pit in its place.  
 
The second level is reached by navigating the Lander down into the pit. In this level, your goal is to land at the 1000 point pad in the cave — a task as hard as it looks. You can control the lander with either a joystick or keyboard. 
 
Game was first published in Ahoy! 1984/04 (Issue #04).

207643.overview:
Dragonspire, home to the ancient order of earth wizards now long since passed into history..

For centuries its great doors have remained closed.

A demon has recently taken control of Dragonspire and is using its magic to bring back the creatures of old.

Dangerous Dragons and orcs, wolves and giants.

Can you find the entrance to the spire, climb the great tower and  defeat the demon before his army of beasts are strong enough to  conquer your homeland.

207748.overview:
Bend it like Beckham with this free-kick mini-game. You have 20 shots to score as many points as possible. Points are awarded for goals scored, the closer to the targets in the net the more points are scored, up to 120 per shot. 

This game was written over a weekend for the C64 Cassette 50 charity competition, where all code and data has to reside below $1000 in memory. Playable in the browser only until the competition is over.

209063.overview:
Luma is a  laser based sliding puzzle game for the Commodore 64. Slide batteries, lasers and mirrors around to light the targets within the given shift count.  With 128 levels Luma will keep you occupied for hours and test your puzzling skills to the max.

Play in Normal mode and try to complete the levels within a designated number of shifts, and return to where you left off using level codes on each level. Or if you are feeling like a more casual game play in Practice mode to test any of the levels with no shift limits. 

Luma was written on a Twitch stream (https://www.twitch.tv/shallan50k) in a marathon 16 hour charity session in support of the Extra Life charity (https://www.extra-life.org/) during which viewers raised an incredible $1220.69 for a very deserving charity. Extra Life unites thousands of gamers around the world to play games in support of their local Children's Miracle Network Hospital. Since its inception in 2008, Extra Life has raised over $70 million USD for sick and injured kids.

209478.overview:
Lazarus is a platform game, where you control a soldier whose mission is to collect 5 items scattered around 5 levels.
