You start the game in a small chamber; when you go to the right, you'll receive info about which item you must bring back, and a code to put into the teleportation machine nearby so that it moves you to one of the levels. The levels are all divided into screens rather than side-scrolling fluidly.

Once you teleport, you must find the item and then make your way to the exit teleporter. On you way, you'll face obstacles: electric barriers, which harm you, and water which kills instantly. Your enemies are two robots (blue and pink) who drop down from the sky in each screen shortly after you enter it. The robots harm you when they touch you, but you can shoot them with your gun. Sometimes, they'll leave behind a bonus, which you can collect to get more health or ammo. The robots walk left and right mindlessly, but can drop down from platforms.

209609.overview:
Law Enforcer is an early 1997 SEUCK game developed by Richard Bayliss and released by The New Dimension.

Instead of your typical scrolling shooter, this is a crosshair shooter in which you have to shoot various criminals inside a building.

210147.overview: Commodore's version of one of the oldest, if not the very oldest computer business management simulations to ever exist. It's the classic lemonade stand simulation that has been around since the 70s done with Commodore flare. The C64 version was a conversion of the PET version. This was included in the Commodore 64 Program Pack that was sold in Canada.

210148.overview: Another interpretation of the classic old school text based business management simulation Lemonade (or Lemonade Stand) This one was developed by Mark D. Rejhon and released into the public domain in 1986. The object is to become a millionaire. You start by selling bottle of lemonade and, if succeeding to make 10k, you proceed to the stock market where you can buy and sell shares to 18 companies.

210232.overview:
This is a deluxe edition of the single button game Little Nippers, which is bigger than the 4K version. The 4K version of this game was originally submitted for the 2022 4K Craptastic Game development competition run by Reset Magazine and Austrogamer.

This is a brand new deluxe version of this game, submitted for the Zzap! 64 Micro Action magazine issue 9's cover mount.

Little Nippers Deluxe consists of the following new features (not featured in the original 4K compo entry): 

-    Loading bitmap
-    Colourful front end presentation
-    Hi score table 
-    Nice summery tunes
-    5 different seaside locations, based on skill level
-    Bonus incentives (Higher skill level, less crabs - more points)
-    Compatible with theC64 mini , theC64, theVIC20 (in c64 mode) full size computer
-    Compatible with both PAL and NTSC, although best played on PAL

The story:

It is Summer time. On the previous day it was a beautiful day for beach-goers, who were swimming in the sea, bathing in the glorious sunshine. That was until it started raining. Everybody had to run for cover, their excuse – they didn't want to get wet. Even the people who were bathing in the sea ran off. A large family of children left 8 buckets on the beach which eventually gets occupied by red migrating crabs.

The migrating crabs were sleeping in the buckets for the night. The next day was a glorious day, with a long-term forecast that it will be sunny all this week. The sleeping crabs get a rude disturbance by a stampede of running kids. This has made the crabs more grumpy and want their revenge on the pesky kids, so they have called on “The Lord of the Crabs”, which of course is you.

Instructions:

This is a funny hi-score attack challenge, which features 8 levels to complete, and 5 skill levels to select from. On the title game options screen, select the skill level to start, and then start the game. The game skill level options are as follows:

-    Skill level 1 = 20 crabs + no bonus per successful nip
-    Skill level 2 = 15 crabs + 2 x score bonus per successful nip
-    Skill level 3 = 10 crabs + 3 x score bonus per successful nip
-    Skill level 4 = 5 crabs + 4 x score bonus per successful nip
-    Skill level 5 = 1 crab + 5 x  score bonus per successful nip

The higher the level, the less bonus points you will get on level completion, due to the limited number of crabs which you have.

How to play:

You have eight buckets lying in line on the beach. There are kids running across the beach at varied speed (depending on the level which you are on). The idea of this game is to use the fire button or the space bar key to launch a crab out of the bucket and move towards its target and nip the kids' feet. 

You will have 10 seconds (which will show on the bucket) to respond, otherwise as a penalty a cross will appear on the bucket and the crab or jellyfish will automatically leave the bucket and go straight into the water without nipping a runner.

210283.overview: Baby UFOs in UFOland have to train arduously before they can leave their homeworld. Historically, the most infamous of these training grounds was the Lei Lei Relay. Collect the lanterns to advance to the next field, up until you reach the UFO cathedral. There you will attain the title of UFO master. LeiLei Relay is a gravity thrust style of game which requires you to guide the UFO using only rotation and thrusters around the game room to collect all the lanterns before you can move onto the next level.

210362.overview: For what is a game made in BASIC this version of Lumberjack by Steveboy aka István Maros is just as enjoyable as all the other versions and as one person on the CSDb rightly says is very playable. The only critique I could give the game is the response time is a little slow, but then that could be down to the C64 forever emulator i'm using on my other computer. Still other than that, i'd highly recommend C64 owners to give this game a go.

210684.overview:
Lighthouse Adventure is a text adventure originally developed by Chris Wilkinson for the TRS-80 Color Computer and published in the book "The Rainbow Book of Adventures". The C64 version was converted by Nathan Butcher. In the late 1700's, an old English ship carrying jewels and gold was seized by pirates in a violent storm. The crew, weak and sick from the long journey, could not properly defend the ship and her invaluable cargo. The pirates killed everyone on board and set sail for America. Months later, they arrived off the coast of a New England peninsula and smuggled the priceless gold on shore. They quickly found a hiding place for the treasure. According to the legend, no one ever found the smugglers or the treasure, but most people believe the gold is located in or near the lighthouse.
 

Over the years, many have tried unsuccessfully to find the legendary gold, but either quit, or died in the quest. This exciting adventure leads you on a magical hunt to find the smugglers hideout, take the treasure and make your getaway. You will encounter many tips along the journey, and here's a helpful one before you begin: The British call it a "trolley," but in America, we call it a "dolly." Happy adventuring!

210685.overview: Lights Out! is a puzzle game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Michael C. Martin and released into the public domain in 2015.

210686.overview: Lights Out! Is a puzzle game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Michael C. Martin, and is an updated version of his 2015 game of the same name. This version was released into the public domain in 2017.

210985.overview: The Labadite Affair is a public domain text adventure for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John Frank. The year of release is unknown.

211251.overview: The mini game Lykia Prologue – Nathan’s Journey takes place before the main game Lykia – The Lost Island and takes us to Rybolido, a small island southeast of Rybola. Great update: PULS4R created an sd2iec version of Lykia Prologue

213393.overview:
Laserland is a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up for the Commodore 64. It was developed and published by Outlaw-Emix Software using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit in 1989.

The game is a bit different from most early SEUCK games in that it features a diaganol/pseudo-isometric playing field.

The game has both single player and two player co-op.

213442.overview:
The beautifully presented adventure features lots of characters to interact with as you help Nora on her magical quest to find the lost island.t's Nora's 16th birthday - but this was to be a birthday like none other!

Sent to pick apothia fruits by her mother something very strange and magical happened when Nora touched the fruit - an ancient spell was disturbed that affected all the people and animals throughout the land!

It also gave Nora special powers! And now it's up to you to discover what is happening and to help various characters that she encounters on her travels.

213701.overview:
The Last Space Ship is a vertcially scrolling shoot 'em up for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Roberto Ricioppo using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit and released by TND in 2013.

The aim of this game is to fly through various zones, zapping away at mutant controlled space crafts. If you get very far, you'll win, otherwise if they succeed to blowing up your last ship. Its all over. Good luck.

213702.overview:
Last Super Ship of Xerox is a vertically scrolling shooter developed by Roberto Ricioppo using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. It was released by TND in 2013.

Fly through the sectors of Xerox and blast the enemy ships to oblivion.

213703.overview:
Little Trains is a horizontally scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Roberto Ricioppo using Jonathan Wells' and Richard Bayliss' sideways SEUCK mod, and released by TND in 2015.

Guide your train across the tracks, and shoot  out the enemy trains before they do the same to you.

213709.overview:
Little Nippers 4K (Entry for the 2022 Reset64 4KB Craptastic Game Competition)
Release date: 1st July 2022
Programming: Richard Bayliss
Graphics: Richard Bayliss, Hugues Poisseroux
Music/SFX: Richard Bayliss
Genre: Arcade - Single button challenge
Tape Loader: Freeload by Paul Hughes (customised)

Crabs were sleeping comfortably in their buckets overnight while it was raining! The next day it is a beautiful day. The crabs were still sleeping until those pesky kids on holiday, start running amok on the beach. The crabs are grumpy and they want to have their revenge.

You are the lord of the crabs using a spacebar or the fire button. The object of this game is to launch your crab onto those pesky kids and nip their feet. If the crab misses their feet, it will end up into the sea, and will be lost. Points scored are based on the distance the crab has to travel. The further the distance, the more number of points it can score. The game is over when all of your crabs are lost.

215974.overview: Based off the original Spanish language selectable answers text adventure from Raúl Morán, this 2014 version was vastly updated with helpful graphics by Igor Errazkin & Raúl Morán and music by Richard Bayliss and later updates in 2017 added an English translation to share the fun with more folks. The latest version was developed by Rulas International under the Sputnik World label. his is a short, but fun adventure game, where the usual system of typing commands to move and examining rooms has been replaced by simply choosing from a few options given at the end of each section.

215975.overview:
An action game, created by Terry L. Flynn and published in Loadstar #135. Bounce a beam off your computer opponent's ship or planet before he bounces you into oblivion. You and your computer opponent are provided with a ship that moves vertically within seven firing positions from which you will fire into crystals spread out at random between the two of you. Your lazer beam may be deflected at 90 degree angles according to where on the crystal you hit. The beam will continue until it hits something other than a crystal ... hopefully his ship or planet. If the lazer beam hits a block, the energy will be absorbed and no damage.  
 
It can take a few minutes to scan all the firing positions to find out which one will end up blowing his ship to space dust. The strategy is to imagine you beam shooting out and follow it as it is deflected by the crystals to see where it ends up. There is no time limit so you can ponder to your heart's content. But beware, your computer opponent will be doing the same!

215976.overview: A single player puzzle\brain game by Barbara H. Schulak & Fender Tucker and published in both Loadstar #140 and Loadstar #189. Have fun playing this word game that uses on-disk dictionaries. You're given a grid of 160 random letters in a 10x16 configuration with a red blank row in the middle. You are to create words on the red row by scrolling the columns up or down. When you think you have a word on the red row reading left to right press return to see if it is in the word list, if so you get one point or every letter in the word. If it is not in the list you get a buzzer!

215977.overview:
The aim of the game is to guide the stickleback through territories where various aquatic creatures live, which will often prove to be very insidious if not even lethal enemies; our stickleback will try to avoid dangerous clashes, to cautiously win the competition of other males of its own species, and finally to find material to be able to build a refuge in which it will attract its mate and thus found a new family. 

Instinct and experience will guide, as occurs in nature, the stickleback in juggling dangers, prey and predators in the eternal game of selecting natural phenomena simulated in this game, it is essential to refer to the enclosed manual. 

Game was originally released in Italy in 1987 in Logica 2000 N°59 and a later English translation was released in 2017.

215978.overview:
A collect-em-up game created by Paul Choquette and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1987/11 (Issue #53). Collect the trash left by aggressive garbage-loving insects in this fast-paced arcade game for the 64. Waste disposal was never this exciting. A joystick and disk drive are required.
It's your first day on the job and you're already considering retirement. Being the city's chief sanitation officer sounded great at first- prestige, a fancy uniform, and even your own official waste receptacle-but no one told you about the bugs. It seems that the city has been infested with a rare breed of giant insects: litterbugs, to be exact. Every time you begin collecting trash, these litterbugs attack, chasing you throughout the city. Talk about an insect problem.
Now, in a high-risk occupation such as litter control, you're bound to run into some trouble now and then. These bugs play dirty: Not only do they litter the streets-if they catch you picking up their trash, they'll soil your uniform. And no self-respecting sanitation officer would be caught dead in a soiled uniform. So, every time a litterbug catches you, you must go back to headquarters, change your uniform, and return to duty. It's a dirty job,

215979.overview: A Sokoban style puzzle game developed by Andreas Laner and published in 64'er 1993/08.

215980.overview:
For some weird reason, as if decided by a million indies, one or more trolleys are stuck in a loop. To break out you need to manually switch crossings. Collect a crystal on every spawn spot to advance to the next stage.

This is a C64 game, so behold the retro goodness! Control is via Joystick in Port 2. Press fire to start game. Move your cursor over a crossing. When it can be toggled the cursor blinks white. Keep the button pushed for any trolley to change direction when passing by. This affects not only your own trolleys (grey), but also the fiendish ones (red).

If one of your trolleys collides with a fiendish one, it’s game over.

All in all there are 10 stages of varying difficulty.

215982.overview:
A Lunar Lander game from the book "Commodore 64 Games Book", created by Clifford Ramshaw & Mark Ramshaw and published by Melbourne House in 1983. This is one for all you budding young astronauts. The surface of the moon is looming closer, and you must control the horizontal and vertical velocities of your module to achieve a feather-light landing.

Keep an eye on your fuel gauge at the bottom of the screen, don’t run out of fuel. The more difficult the landing site the more points you get for a successful mission, each perfect landing increases the difficulty of the next. Be careful not to damage your module by landing too hard.

215990.overview: Leisure Suit Leo II: The Secret of Maniac Island is a German language Commodore 64 graphics/text adventure game released in 1997 by Out of Order. A text adventure with graphics created by  Stephan Lesch and Tobias Erbsland of Volker Rust as a parody of the adult themed Leisure Suit Larry series. A preview version was also released in GO64! 1998/01. An English version was later created but not published.

216004.overview: A single player shooter\bomber game a.k.a. "Lunar Blitz Remix" released in the  Reset #04 Mix-i-Disk. This game by Jason Kelk and Matt Simmonds of Cosine Systems and was released in 2014.

216318.overview: Collect'em up with ASCII graphics. Your goal is to gather as much gold as possible in two minutes while avoiding mummies and snakes.

216437.overview:
Star Klondike (also Known as Loadstar's Klondike Solitaire) is a variation of Klondike solitaire for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John Serafino and published in Loadstar #138 in 1995.

The game has several options, including the ability for drawing 1 or 3 cards, as well as the ability to play either a single-deck or a double-deck version of the game.

217116.overview: The Last Fighter is a 1-2 player co-operative vertcially scrolling shmup for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Commodore 64 Live using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit (SEUCK) and released in an unknown year to the public domain)

217123.overview:
The Last Gate is a miscellaneous shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by DiBi Soft and published only in Italy in Next Game #04 (04/1985). 

In this game, you control a stationary tank in the middle of the screen, which can only move the tank's turret. Enemies come from all sides of the screen, so be careful where you aim your turret.

Almost like a fixed-screen Tempest variant in a way.

217207.overview: A horizontally scrolling shoot-em up preview game created by Stuart A. Cook and released as a preview in Digital Marketing PD #023 that would be reworked and modified, then eventually published under another name by Bug-Byte software. This version would never see release outside the preview copies.

217352.overview: An Italian text adventure, The Secret Valley from Andrea Pecorari  with music by Fausto Mazzoni. You are standing in front of the entrance to your friend Joe's house. Joe called you to show you his latest adventure. You see a closed door, there is a doorbell...what will you do next?

218106.overview:
La Sala Degli Enigmi is a 1985 Italian language miscellaneous genre game, including a  shoot em up for the Commodore 64. The coder is unknown. It was published in Videoteca Computer #09. The game is keyboard control only. 
 
THE ROOM OF PUZZLES: You have finally arrived at the conclusion of the trio of games useful for saving the princess: what a struggle to be a hero! To conclude your mission which has gradually become more daring, you just have to pass the last tests. A good rider must undoubtedly possess three essential requirement: have excellent aim, exhibit exceptional reflexes, and of course have some luck!
Here is the first test:

La Mira:Hit the ghostly figures that appear with the magic stars. The movements you have available are governed by the following keys: Z M which allows you to move to the left which allows you to move to the right BAR/SPACE to shootBe careful because to obtain the information you are interested in you must be able, as always, to pass the test more than brilliantly.

Second test: THE REFLECTIONS:Evil spirits of an ancient warrior, of the magician and of the ever-present ghost of the castle, appear evanescent and very rapid in the room of puzzles: you have to identify them and, precisely with quick reflexes, fix them on the screen by pressing the relative keys:
M for the wizard, F for ghost and G for warrior. It must be admitted that it is not easy at all, but after all being heroes is not a trivial matter.
If you overcome even this difficult undertaking, all you have to do is give "checkmate" also to...

FATE: following the instructions you will have to beat your enemy by contrasting the ghostly figures that he summons to destroy you with the right counterpart. Be careful because in order not to start over you will have to be exceptionally fast.
Finally, if you heroically win, don't think it's over: you can use your ingenuity to solve the mystery and finally receive the dazzling image of the castle you won at a great price. Well admit it, wasn't it worth it?

218671.overview: Make your way through an underground labyrinth of an anthill-like configuration, blasting the insects that bug you. Find your way to the final chambers, if you can find them!

219160.overview: Another cute mini game from Japanese dev Inufuto released on 12.29.2021!  This game may look simple to the eye, but it's extremely addictive and fun!  It's a bit of a mash-up between a puzzler version of Elevator Action and Capture the Flag!  To maximize scoring, pick up consecutive color flags!  Inufutu posts all of his games on approximately 27 different retro computer formats.

219425.overview:
In the game, you were to control a young Lord of the castle-in-the-sky, where you have inherited a mighty winged steed and a powerful fire-staff, but more importantly the hand of a beautiful princess in marriage.

Furious at being overlooked on the wedding guest list, a coven of witches steal and lock her away in a distant tower and cast your staff deep into a volcano. Heartbroken, you head eastward on a quest to save her.

The game would take place across 6 distinct locations overall, including: The Wood, The Volcano, The Battle, The Cerulean Caves, The Well and The Coven. It was a neat and ambitious first development by Jeremy, all crammed into a single load and developed over a 2-3 month period.

219468.overview:
6th June 2182, Mars

The Space Station Factory orbiting the planet is undergoing an unprecedented mutiny.
The main computer of the space station UNSS ASAMI has gone rougue during decommissioning and gained control of the guardian droids.
After winning a short battle with the UN army dislocated on Mars, the rebellious mainframe is now pointing the station towards earth with its load of uncontained radioactive material.

You are the android L-3573-R, the first of a new generation of guardian droids independent from a central AI.  Given your strenghts, you are the only hope to stop this threat and figure out what happened to the station.

GOOD LUCK!

 FEATURES
- An entire space station to explore
- 60+ rooms full of metroidvania action
- Upgradable weapon, special powers, map and inventory
- 11 tracks OST
- THEC64 (Maxi and mini) compatibility

219692.overview: Logomix is a single-player logical game developed by Steffen Schloßhauer. It was published in 64'er 1992/06. Think, consider and execute. That's roughly the motto of the game Logomix. It's about bringing the stones scattered on the left side back into shape, i.e. sorting them exactly as shown on the right half of the screen. It all sounds very simple, you might be thinking. However, you cannot move the stones around as you wish, you can only turn four of them clockwise at the same time. An additional limitation of the moves makes it even more difficult, because in some levels a certain order is important so that you don't run out of moves halfway. By the way, the controls are provided by a joystick in port 2. The stones can be rotated with the fire button.

219782.overview:
If you're in the mood for a challenging and addictive word game, please check out Logos64.  Logos64 is a C64 port of the hit game Wordle.  The latest version of logos64 features:

    A database of nearly 6,000 words.
    Instant validation of guesses - no wait time required.
    Two game types - the daily game or a random game.

 
logos64 also features cumulative statistics tracked for each player (saved to disk):

    Total number of games played.
    Percentage of games won.
    Current winning streak.
    Highest winning streak.
    Guess distribution.

219807.overview:
It's Santa's final job to save the worlds last snowball from hitting the water and melting forever!!!!

Can Santa do it?!

Every 100 points the snowball gets faster, when will Santa tire out...how long can he protect the worlds last snowball!!

219813.overview:
The Daring Rescue of Pacuvia the Sheep is a short, bizarre, traditional interactive fiction game for C64, Amiga, MS-Dos, Windows and Tandy Model 100. But it's also something more, it's a - drumroll - sentimental research project!

Your character is an operative of a mysterious “Agency”, on a dangerous mission: rescuing the bioengineered sheep called Pacuvia from the clutches of a guy too idiot to understand what he's got. Strapped of all your digital support for security reasons, you'll have to rely on your good ol' analogic equipment to recover Pacuvia. And don't forget she's not necessarily helpless...

219821.overview: Little Spider is a solitaire game created by Maurice Jones and published in Loadstar #149 in 1996. In little spider, the reserve is evenly divided under ten tableau piles. It is similar in some aspects to the standard Spider game, but much more difficult. A true challenge from the Loadstar master of Solitaire.

219850.overview: You Escaped the City and headed towards the mountains, Here you find a hidden Door, you peek inside, Looks like some sort of Bunker, Could it be safe here, You Enter the door.

219851.overview:
Kill the Zombies and try to survive.

Push Move Side Scrolling Shoot 'em' Up, Made to be fun and not a Hard Game.

219974.overview: The Lost Caves 11 is a version of Boulder Dash created by Lars Bernhofen aka schlonkel based on the original work of Peter Liepa. It supports one or two players and was released at Gamescom 2016 in Cologne.  It has 30 new caves to explore.

219984.overview: The Lost Caves 9 is a version of Boulder Dash created by Lars Bernhofen aka schlonkel based on the original work of Peter Liepa. It supports one or two players and was released in 2014. It has 30 new caves to explore.

219987.overview: The Lost Caves 10 is a version of Boulder Dash created by Lars Bernhofen aka schlonkel based on the original work of Peter Liepa. It supports one or two players and was released in 2015.  It has 30 new caves to explore.

220116.overview:
In Landmine the player must traverse a 10 by 10 field of possible mine locations, from top left to bottom right. The program sets up an almost too easy first two or three attempts but the machine is programmed to place the mines randomly increasing the numbers of mines by 2 each time. Rapidly the player is faced with the near impossible task of negotiating 48, 50 and more mines. The program does offer the player a little help, in that it issues a warning whenever the player is one and/or two moves away from being blown to smithereens.

In giving the reader (and eventual user), the bare outlines of this addictive game, a lot of scope opens up for the ambitious and inventive home programmer. In this quiet utility program, he can create a more attractive display and with the increased sound capabilities of the 64 develop an exciting range of explosive
sounds and warnings. 
 
A game created by Richard Franklin and published in the book "CBM 64 Programs - Volume 1" in 1984.

220154.overview: Luna 3 (also spelled as Luna III) is a side scrolling space shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed and released by Spanish developers Sputnik World on January 7, 2017. The game is available in both English and Spanish language versions.

310686.overview:
Linko is a Mastermind variant for the Commodore 64. It was developed vy Visual Delight (consisting of Roland Hermans on cod, Hermans and Willy Voesten, and Joachim Wijnhoven on music/SFX) the game was published in GO64! 2002/05.

However, unlike most Mastermind variants, you play for money, as a type of "game show" against either the computer, or a second player.

The game is playable in three different languages: English, German, and Dutch.

311150.overview: Line-Up is a single-player numerical puzzle game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Robert B. Cook, and published in the October 1990 issue of COMPUTE!'s Gazette (during this time, the magazine was in the regular COMPUTE! Magazine as an insert, rather than sold as a standalone magazine).

311185.overview:
This was a planned sequel to Cosmos Designs' side scrolling shooter, Lions of the Universe. The game was never finished, but a playable demo version was discovered years later and placed on GTW64 (Games That Weren't 64). The game was being developed during 1994 (the year that the original was released)

The game was supposed to be released by Cherry Software when it was completed.

417734.overview: Lost Realms of Murkasada: Episode 2 is a brand new freeware adventure game with role-playing elements for the Commodore 64. It was released on April 8, 2023 and developed by Arkanix Labs. It is a companion/side adventure/rpg-lite of their development C64 CRPG Crimson Twilight which they are currently working on.

417979.overview: A PD single screen, arcade style, fantasy themed platformer that was created by Pasi Hytönen and released in 1986 and later re-released by "Komoda & Amiga plus" in 2018. Well in Little Knight Arthur, you are on a quest to defeat the evil Shamrock The Dragon. On the way, you will need to collect and use weapons and also figure out how to free your friends captured by Shamrock's evil gang which includes bats, spiders, snakes, and even undead creatures! This will involve a lot of jumping, platform hoping and rope climbing. So be fast or you'll die a lot!

418058.overview:
THE SHADOKS... IT'S CRAZY...With his famous and hilarious cartoon, Jacques Rouxel invents one of the greatest "laughing pumps" in the history of television. But one day computer scientists decided to make you participate in the crazy epic of the curious little characters. 

So, if you have breath, nerves of steel, excellent reflexes; here is for you, the first volume of a long series of delirious arcades, where you will have to jump, fly, pump and run upside down as well as downside up!

418222.overview:
Classics from the Past! A title that should not be missed if you wish to experience Retrogaming at its finest.(Maybe Im biased?) Last Ninja was initially developed for the C64 and later to many computers like ZX Spectrum, Atari, Amiga and even PCs. So successful it led to 2 more sequels and a Remix. Now you can experience all 4 titles in 1 cartridge.  
 
 The plot is simple for these titles, you play ninja Armakuni ordered to assassinate an evil shogun Kunitoki at his castle (Last Ninja), then travel through time to 20th century to fight him again (Last Ninja 2) and finally at his retreat hideout in Tibet.(Last Ninja 3)

The Last Ninja is a beautiful game with good music and features a blend of exploration, puzzle solving, and combat gameplay. Like old computers, these are not easy games (Damm the rocks in the river) but completing it is rewarding.

418365.overview: Laser Invaders is a side scrolling space shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Ted Dallas and released into the public domain in 2021.

418517.overview: The year is 2073. A hostile alien race has arrived on earth, after crossing countless star systems, with the aim of taking over the planet. Initially taken by surprise, humanity managed to react and organize a resistance that made it possible to fend off various enemy attacks. However, this was not enough to repel the alien invader who is now about to carry out his plans for conquest. Only one last brave hero is left to fight. The entire human species is now counting on him to defeat the enemy and regain their freedom.

418768.overview:
As a pilot, you've heard of all the dangers of reconnaisance missions: radar defense systems, land-based barriers, and worst of all, missiles. Although regular missiles are troubIe enough for reconnaisance pilots, heat-seeking missiles are their greatest problem.

All this talk never meant anything to you until you were picked to lead a reconnaisance mission through enemy territory. The code name for the mission is LARC-1. You'll be flying the government's experimental L.A.R.C. prototype (for Low Altitude Reconnaisance Craft). The terrain you'll be flying over is covered with radar placements, pylons, and walls. Walls have large holes which your craft can pass through. There are also heat-seeking missiles that home in on the heat from your ship's exhaust. The only way to stop a heat-seeker is to cause it to collide with an obstacle.

419521.overview:
Ladybug is a C64 conversion of the maze game "Lady Bug" which was brought into the arcade halls by the company UNIVERSAL in 1981 and which was one of the successful followers of the famous Pac-Man.

The aim of the game is to "eat" all the flowers (points) and the bonus flower with the pawn, a ladybug (or ladybird), and reach as many points as possible. You start the game with three bugs (lives).

The pawn is disturbed in its task by four hostile insects that emerge one after the other from their nest in the centre of the maze. Their speed rises in the course of the game. When the last insect has left its nest, a vegetable appears in the middle of the maze which gives bonus points when it is collected.

In the maze next to the normal flowers also several bonus flowers with letters and hearts are scattered. You get an extra life or 10.000 bonus points when you make it to put together the words „EXTRA“ or „SPECIAL“. If you eat a flower with a heart, a multiplicator is switched on that doubles all other points that come after that, the second heart triples them and the third even quintuples them.

The game has another special feature which differentiates from the known Pac-Man: these are 20 green revolving doors with which Ladybug can changed the maze. The "evil one's" cannot turn the doors. The skillful turning of the doors is the only possibility for Ladybug to escape the followers; because the bug's speed stays the same in all levels, while the speed for the enemies rises. You should close the doors quickly when you are chased by a follower; if it comes too close to Ladybug, the turning door will not have any use: The "evil guy" will also slip through and get the Lady.

The skulls that are on the field mean death to the Ladybug and also for its opponents. The player loses a life (one ladybug) when running into a skull. The other insects are transported back to their nest in the centre and get into the game when the timer has run down again.

The timer is an interrupted white stripe that runs around the game area. When the lady bug has entered the maze, the single elements of this stripe change their colour in clockwise order: they get green starting at the top. When all elements of the stripe are green, the first opponent leaves its nest and the next round starts; all elements get white again one after the other. The speed of the timer rises with rising levels.

422551.overview: Last Ninja IV is an unreleased prototype (playable demo) game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jon Wells and Paul "Feekzoid" Hannay. 441496.overview:
This game is an unofficial C64 port of Lock'n'Chase from LC-Games, an arcade game developed by DECO in 1981.

Game Description:

Lock 'n' Chase is an arcade action game similar to Pac-Man. You play a thief who is trapped in a maze like vault. To get out, you need to collect all of the gold dots located in the maze. Your task won't be easy, since there are four police officers in the vault who are constantly trying to catch you! Located throughout the maze are numerous doors. As you run through the maze, you have the ability to temporarily close a door in an attempt to block the police. You can only close two doors at a time, and any closed doors automatically open again after a short amount of time. When all of the gold in the maze has been collected, the exit to the vault will open and you can escape and move on to the next, more difficult vault. Occasionally a bonus item will appear in the maze, such as a cash bag, crown, or briefcase, which can be collected to earn even more points.

444255.overview:
Behold a magical adventure through time and space.   Ulrich the arch wizard has finally achieved his lifetime work of discovering all the locations of the fabled Dragon Amulet pieces. But he's so old now, who is going to help Ulrich fetch the pieces of the Dragon Amulet?

The game is an unofficial sequel/update to the game Kokotoni Wilf.

447268.overview: Little Dragon: Cookie Raiders is a catch-it style game in which you play a green dragon at the bottom of the screen. Your goal is to move the dragon across the screen and catch the cookies in your basket as they drop. The game was developed by Jamie Sampson using Garry Kitchen's GameMaker and released into the public domain in 2007.

448159.overview: A game in the trilogy of zombie horror text adventure games ported from the ZX BASIC version by Carmine Migliaccio in 2024. Original game was in Italian, the ports are in english and some graphics have limited movement.  The game’s title, “La Casa”, is inspired by the movie series Evil Dead by Sam Raimi.

448591.overview:
Cops and Robbers is a two-player game originally published in "The Commodore 64 Games Book - 21 Sensational Games." One player controls the cops, while the other controls the robbers. The goal for the cops is to chase and catch the robbers in the city before they escape to their hideout.

The city streets run north to south and east to west. The cops have faster cars but must obey traffic laws, allowing only forward or left turns at intersections, with no right turns or U-turns. The robbers can ignore traffic laws, giving them better maneuverability despite having slower cars.

Players can choose the speed of the game. At its fastest, it becomes a thrilling chase through the streets. Played more slowly, it becomes a game of strategy.

449056.overview:
Rev your engine - it's time to do some racing!

Try your driving skills against the meanest, leanest, sleekest road machines around. Put your Diablo to the test as you race, avoid bad-attitude cops, and put the skids on your opponents. Bet enough money and win, and you'll be able to upgrade your car...or maybe you'll just lose it all. Think you can handle the drive?

452688.overview:
Not to be confused with the Amiga game of the same name (which is a German language quiz game), Lyris for the Commodore 64 is a 1-player Tetris/Columns variant.

The game was developed by Andreas Föhl and published in Golden Disk 64 #04 (1989)

453467.overview:
Damn you...damn you all to hell… New York, London, Paris, Munich… you blew it all up! The bad guys won and the world is now a wasteland.

But maybe all is not lost. You are the last secret agent with the last Z-8 time machine. The city is riddled with ghosts and the time door won’t open before you have accumulated a major zonk overload.

Use joystick in Port 2. Fire launches missiles or traps, when appropriate. On the map screen, guide the car towards the ghosts. After that, generally, avoid touching anything with your car or your person.

The free demo version was published in ZZAP! 64 Micro Action Issue #22.   It is limited to 2 simultaneous human players.  The full version of the game supports players 3 and 4 with User Port adapter.  Made by Jess Peterson aka FuzzyBad aka Jess in 2024.

455775.overview: Momma Ladybird was out one day with the kiddies, eating aphids, chilling out on leaves, you know, usual ladybird stuff.

457109.overview:
Lincoln Green is a simple top-down action-adventure game for the Commodore 64. Dodge the arrows, but keep a close hold on the loot in a mad rush to safety through an enchanted forest. For the 64. Joystick required.

There’s nothing more beautiful than an enchanted forest. Unfortunately, there’s also nothing more dangerous. | You, Lincoln Green, defender of the poor, are on the run from the sheriff of Nottingham after having stolen £600 of gold dust from a nobleman. In your haste, you have accidentally slipped into Enchanted Forest instead of the nearby Sherwood forest.

It was developed by Roberto Bixby and published as a type-in game in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/09 (Issue #63).

460712.overview: The New Dimension is very proud to bring to you a fun Space Invaders inspired game called "Let's Invade 3", which was originally made as part of the Scene World issue 36 game coding tutorial "Let's Make a C64 Game".

William Tell is a platform shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by David W. Light where your aim is to rescue the apple of his eye, his son.

The first stage of the game involves the collection of two keys which unlock the doors to the dungeons. Both keys are lo be found hanging up outside the guardroom* located at either end of the battlements. The battlements are patrolled by armed guards who can either be shot with your crossbow or jumped over if your timing's good. Occasionally you must replenish your supply of crossbow bolts by jumping up and collecting them. Timing your jump is vital because arrows and cannonballs are whittling overhead. Once you've got the keys, fight your way back to the ladder m\d then you can descend to the courtyard.

This game was published in the following:

- Your Commodore 1988/11
- Your Commodore 1989/01
- Your Commodore 1989/03

462543.overview: After Santa failed to save the last snowball the world went into extreme drought and now the following fall only one pumpkin remains.....the last pumpkin!

463546.overview:
You are a lunar researcher. You now find yourself on a planet whose moon, called "Lunadia," has collided with an asteroid and collapsed. There is little time left to escape the disaster, but even less time to recover your research.

The game was made with GKGM (Garry Kitchen's GameMaker)

463756.overview:
Constructing a maze is a common task in video game design. The simplest approach is to define a fixed maze layout by assigning a specific character to each screen position; however, this means the player always faces the same maze and quickly learns it by heart.

To avoid this issue, the program can be designed to generate a unique maze each time it is run.

Another drawback—particularly relevant to small computers—is the limited screen space available for displaying the maze. The program presented here overcomes this limitation, making the game as engaging as possible.

Published in the Italian type-in book "20 Programmi per Commodore 64".

463787.overview:
In a Tibetan monastery—so an ancient Eastern legend goes—there are three rods fixed into the floor of a room; at the beginning of the world, 64 concentric disks were arranged on the first rod, with the smallest ones resting atop the larger ones. Since the dawn of time, monks have been moving one disk at a time from one rod to another, aiming to transfer the entire stack to a different rod, all while ensuring that a larger disk is never placed upon a smaller one. According to the legend, the world will end when the monks complete their task.

For our purposes, we will limit the height of our towers to a maximum of 8 disks. Our program must be capable of displaying the initial stack of disks and the movement of a single disk from one stack to another on the screen; it must accept and execute our moves—verifying their validity—and signal when we have successfully moved the entire stack, thereby solving the problem. 
 
Published in the book "20 Programmi per Commodore 64"

463789.overview:
With this program, we present a solitaire puzzle that requires both thought and effort. The game involves placing eight queens on a chessboard so that none of them threatens another. Anyone familiar with chess knows that the queen can move horizontally, vertically, and diagonally; since a chessboard consists of 8 × 8 = 64 squares, it might seem impossible to place all eight queens without any two of them attacking each other. In reality, there are about seventy different solutions to the problem (excluding symmetries and rotations), yet the player will soon discover that finding even one is not so easy. 
 
Published in the Italian type-in book "20 Programmi per Commodore 64".

I came with two colleagues with whom I have been studying and contrasting data from the area for some time to locate the tomb of Imhotep and we have clues that lead us to think that he lies buried very close to the step pyramid of Djoser, right here in Saqqara and south of this one, about 500 meters away. 482762.overview: Larry has to work his way through monster filled levels trying to avoid being hit by them. How much health you lose will be determined by the difficulty setting you play on. To help with the monsters, there are lots of yummy items you can eat.
